datasets.name: city_sales
queryLines:
WITH relevant_rollup AS (
  SELECT
    city,
    SUM(total_pieces_sold) AS total_pieces_sold,
    SUM(gross_sales_volume) AS gross_sales_volume,
    SUM(total_effective_sales_volume) AS total_effective_sales_volume,
    MAX(max_discount) AS city_max_discount
  FROM
    sales_data_cc.gold.task1_sales_rollup
  WHERE
    (
      :product_section IS NULL
      OR array_contains(:product_section, section)
    )
    AND (
      :product_season IS NULL
      OR array_contains(:product_season, season)
    )
    AND (
      :sale_month IS NULL
      OR array_contains(:sale_month, sale_month)
    )
  GROUP BY
    city
),
city_product_counts AS (
  -- Exact per-city distinct products cannot be re-combined from the rollup,
  -- so this one column still reads the sale-grain fact view.
  SELECT
    city,
    COUNT(DISTINCT product_id) AS relevant_product_count
  FROM
    sales_data_cc.gold.task1_sales_facts
  WHERE
    (
      :product_section IS NULL
      OR array_contains(:product_section, section)
    )
    AND (
      :product_season IS NULL
      OR array_contains(:product_season, season)
    )
    AND (
      :sale_month IS NULL
      OR array_contains(:sale_month, sale_month)
    )
  GROUP BY
    city
)
SELECT
  r.city,
  CAST(r.total_effective_sales_volume AS DOUBLE) AS total_effective_sales_volume,
  r.total_pieces_sold,
  c.relevant_product_count,
  CAST(r.total_effective_sales_volume AS DOUBLE) AS actual_discount_sales_volume,
  CAST(r.gross_sales_volume * (1 - r.city_max_discount) AS DOUBLE) AS max_discount_sales_volume,
  r.city_max_discount,
  CAST(
    r.gross_sales_volume * (1 - r.city_max_discount) - r.total_effective_sales_volume AS DOUBLE
  ) AS volume_difference
FROM
  relevant_rollup r
  LEFT JOIN city_product_counts c
    ON c.city = r.city
ORDER BY
  r.city

datasets.name: monthly_rate
datasets.displayName: Findings - Pieces per Day by Month
queryLines:
SELECT
  DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', s.sale_ts) AS sale_month,
  COUNT(DISTINCT DATE(s.sale_ts)) AS days_with_data,
  SUM(s.pieces_sold) AS pieces_sold,
  ROUND(SUM(s.pieces_sold) / COUNT(DISTINCT DATE(s.sale_ts)), 0) AS pieces_per_day
FROM
  sales_data_cc.silver.sales s
    JOIN sales_data_cc.silver.products p
      ON s.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE
  (
    :product_section IS NULL
    OR array_contains(:product_section, p.section)
  )
  AND (
    :product_season IS NULL
    OR array_contains(:product_season, p.season)
  )
  AND (
    :sale_month IS NULL
    OR array_contains(:sale_month, s.sale_month)
  )
GROUP BY
  1
ORDER BY

datasets.displayName: Findings - Avg Pieces by Discount Decile
queryLines:
SELECT
  ROUND(FLOOR(f.discount * 10) / 10, 1) AS discount_decile,
  COUNT(*) AS sale_rows,
  ROUND(AVG(f.pieces_sold), 2) AS avg_pieces_sold
FROM
  sales_data_cc.gold.task1_sales_facts f
WHERE

    :product_section IS NULL

  AND (
    :product_season IS NULL
    OR array_contains(:product_season, f.season)
  )
  AND (
    :sale_month IS NULL
    OR array_contains(:sale_month, f.sale_month)
  )
GROUP BY
  1
ORDER BY

datasets.name: discount_histogram
queryLines:
WITH sale_keys AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    product_id,
    city,
    sale_month
  FROM
    sales_data_cc.silver.sales
),
labelled AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN d.discount = 0 THEN 0.0
      ELSE ROUND(FLOOR(d.discount * 20) / 20, 2)
    END AS discount_value,
    CASE
      WHEN d.discount = 0 THEN '0% (exact)'
      ELSE
        CONCAT(
          LPAD(CAST(LEAST(CAST(FLOOR(d.discount * 20) AS INT), 3) * 5 AS STRING), 2, '0'),
          '–',
          LPAD(CAST(LEAST(CAST(FLOOR(d.discount * 20) AS INT), 3) * 5 + 5 AS STRING), 2, '0'),
          '%'
        )
    END AS discount_range,
    CONCAT(d.product_id, '|', d.city) AS product_city
  FROM
    sales_data_cc.silver.discounts d
      JOIN sales_data_cc.silver.products p
        ON d.product_id = p.product_id
      LEFT JOIN sale_keys k
        ON k.product_id = d.product_id
        AND k.city = d.city
  WHERE
    (
      :product_section IS NULL
      OR array_contains(:product_section, p.section)
    )
    AND (
      :product_season IS NULL
      OR array_contains(:product_season, p.season)
    )
    AND (
      :sale_month IS NULL
      OR array_contains(:sale_month, k.sale_month)
    )
)
SELECT
  discount_value,
  discount_range,
  COUNT(DISTINCT product_city) AS row_count
FROM
  labelled
GROUP BY
  1,
  2
ORDER BY
  1,

# Filtering this page — defaults reproduce Task 1's winter scope

Every widget on this page reacts to the **Product section**, **Product season** and **Sale month** filters in the filter sidebar. The filters open on **WOMAN / WINTER / January–February** — Task 1's winter scope (the data has no December).

* **Scenario 1 — winter by product season:** Product section = WOMAN, Product season = WINTER, Sale month = all months
* **Scenario 2 — winter by sale month:** Product section = WOMAN, Sale month = 2025-01 and 2025-02 (december is missing from the data), Product season = all seasons
* **Scenario 3 — combined: winter by product season:** Product section = WOMAN, Product season = WINTER and **winter by sale month:** Sale month = 2025-01 and 2025-02 (december is missing from the data)

To widen a filter back to everything, select every option in it. Task 1b always recomputes each **city max discount within the current selection**, so the actual-vs-max comparison matches exactly what you have filtered to. The Key Findings page follows the same filters.

# Task 1 & 1b — what this page explains

Every widget here follows the same **Product section**, **Product season** and **Sale month** filters as the City Sales page, so the findings below describe exactly the data behind your current selection — not the full year.

* **Task 1** — effective sales volume per city: pieces sold × price × (1 − discount), for the selected scope.
* **Task 1b** — the same sales re-priced at each city's maximum available discount; the difference is volume the deeper uniform discount would give away.

The counters below summarize the current selection, and the charts underneath explain the patterns driving those numbers (flat monthly rate, no weekday seasonality, near-uniform discounts, no demand elasticity).
